summary.headline: UBL Q2 FY27: net sales up 24% and EBITDA up 108% to a 11.9% margin, helped by a ~36 crore one-off tax-refund interest in other income.
summary.overview: Volumes grew 16% YoY and net sales 24%, with premium volumes up 38% led by Heineken Silver (+67%) and Ultra (+44%). EBITDA margin rose 480 bps to 11.9% and EBIT margin reached 8.4%; management said ~36 crore of interest income on a tax refund sits in other income and flatters the quarter, with underlying margin expansion still ~330 bps. Management said Q2 is not a run-rate: it guided volume growth to moderate sequentially next quarter as commercial spend and capacity investments step up, and gross margin to 43-45%.

financial_highlights.metric: One-off interest income on tax refund (other income)

segments.name: Premium portfolio
segments.commentary: Premium volumes grew 38% YoY; Heineken Silver grew 67% (sold in 11 states, produced in four local breweries) and Ultra grew 44% after localisation and packaging relaunch. Premium portfolio was growing ~15% at the start of the year.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Volumes grew more than 60% YoY after the state's low-alcohol beer tax cut; management cites ~250 bps market share gain there. Karnataka is 11-12% of business.

segments.name: Maharashtra
segments.commentary: Named with Karnataka as the main state driver of the quarter's price/mix; growth above 50% cited for the state.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: Growth around 40% for UBL, aided by retail policy liberalisation annualisation; premium portfolio not yet produced locally there.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected in the 43-45% range for the next couple of quarters as input cost pressure persists.
Full-year FY27 gross impact from input costs revised to 350-400 crore, slightly lower than the May estimate, after mitigation.
Volume growth expected to moderate sequentially next quarter as commercial spend normalises against a low base and investment is stepped up ahead of next summer.
Structural impact of gross pricing plus trade rationalisation estimated at 200-300 bps of net sales growth.
Long-term volume outlook 6-7% for the category, absent further policy change.
Commercial spend on brands up ~20% YTD versus prior year, growing ahead of revenue and volume.
capex_capacity: Two new canning lines coming up this quarter.
Greenfield and brownfield investments in progress (UP expansion and one more locally) to bring more volume to own breweries.
Two breweries in Tamil Nadu with capital investment to scale up, including new capacity.
Own breweries are ~70-75% of production; the rest comes from contract breweries, with eight additional CBUs onboarded since the new CEO joined.
Supply chain in India not fully geared for disproportionate growth; investment in capacity is needed ahead of next summer.
demand_pricing: Pricing actions taken across 24 markets, a higher count than before; about 30% of business (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu named) has not yet had a price increase.
Net sales price/mix contributed ~8 points: over 50% pricing and trade rationalisation, ~300 bps state mix, ~50 bps operating model mix.
Operating model mix swung from a 400-600 bps drag last year to a ~50 bps gain this quarter as more volume was made in own breweries.
Category growing at double digits; volume growth 6.2% on a three-year and 6% on a two-year basis.
Telangana set up a pricing committee led by a judge; UBL made a cost submission in August. Outcome uncertain.
Commercial spend and competitive intensity rising; management says the industry is seeing more players targeting India volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Karnataka and Jharkhand growth is UBL share gain versus category growth, and what choices drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Karnataka category growth is ~50%, with UBL growing 60%+ and gaining ~250 bps of share; Karnataka is 11-12% of business. Management cited a revenue management programme (state, SKU, brand and trade spend choices) and said it is walking away from low-margin trade spend in states like Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: Which large states have not yet seen price increases, and what does that imply for pure pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of business, including Karnataka's neighbour Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu, has no price increase yet; these are awaiting government processes. Management said pricing is combined with trade spend cuts and SKU mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is the push-to-pull brand investment shift margin-neutral in the short run?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trade-term savings are reinvested behind brands, moving spend from top line to cost, so gross margin expands but short-term operating margin is roughly unchanged; long-term it builds sustained brand-led demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the quarter-by-quarter gross margin bridge and FY27 cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year FY27 gross input-cost impact revised to 350-400 crore (slightly lower than May). Mitigation includes pricing, trade rationalisation and productivity; management said margins should stay in 43-45% for the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Volume outlook and tailwinds for coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the category growth driver is policy change; the base outlook is 6-7% volume growth absent a dramatic policy move, and the Karnataka policy effect will cycle from May-June next year.

qa_highlights.question: Heineken Silver potential and whether Karnataka-type price cuts could be repeated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees Heineken Silver as a potential leading premium brand over time, and that price cuts without a policy change are not the plan; the Karnataka move followed a tax reduction on low-alcohol beer.

risks_watch: About 36 crore one-off interest income flatters Q2; underlying run-rate is lower than headline.
Sequential moderation in volume growth next quarter as commercial and capacity investments rise.
Input costs (Middle East-linked, sugar, other commodities) remain elevated; management does not expect quick easing and does not expect pre-war pricing to return.
Telangana pricing committee outcome and timing; Tamil Nadu policy change still in flux.
Rising competition from new players in premium and mainstream segments; some competitors chasing volume through trade spend.
Dependence on state policy (Karnataka tax cut, Maharashtra) for category growth; cycling of Karnataka base from May-June next year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the strategy, but explicitly cautious on sustainability: management repeatedly said Q2 is not a run-rate, that the path is non-linear, and that it will spend more in Q3. Evasive when asked for peer comparisons (declined to compare margins with Carlsberg or other listed brewers) and on the Telangana pricing outcome.

we expect margins to remain among the range of 48 to 45%, which I think is a good number for everyone, so you keep in mind.
So we are going to make investments in this quarter.
I can tell you that's currently not anything which is happening as we speak but it's how this footprint will evolve is something that we track on a continuous basis.

Step up investment in capacity ahead of next summer

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided at 43-45% for the next couple of quarters (vs 44.7% in Q2 and 41% in Q1), but the ~36 crore tax-refund interest flatters Q2 and underlying expansion is ~330 bps, with commercial spend rising and Q3 spend step-up flagged, so EBITDA margin is unlikely to hold at 11.9%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two canning lines coming up this quarter (Q2) and UP and other brewery expansions under construction, with management saying supply chain is not geared for growth and capacity is needed ahead of next summer; own breweries run at 70-75% of production.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management held 6-7% FY27 volume outlook, but Q2 grew 16% (Q1: 9%) and premium volumes rose 38%; sequential moderation is guided next quarter, so growth is likely to step down from 16% toward the 6-7% base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said it is raising capital investment to scale Tamil Nadu breweries including new capacities, and that investment is needed ahead of next summer; own breweries are 70-75% of production with eight extra CBUs onboarded.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 volume outlook was held at 6-7% and gross margin guided at 43-45% for the next couple of quarters; management called Q2 not a run-rate and said volume growth will moderate next quarter.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Volume growth is guided to moderate sequentially, commercial spend on brands is up ~20% YTD, and Telangana (about 30% of business) has no price increase yet and faces an uncertain pricing committee outcome.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launch was discussed; Heineken Silver and Ultra were cited as growth drivers but no new launch was named.

rows.label: Price increases in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu (~30% of business)
rows.why: About 30% of business has not had a price increase yet; these depend on government processes, and Telangana's pricing committee outcome is uncertain, so a pricing step-up could add to the 200-300 bps structural pricing and trade-rationalisation benefit.

rows.label: FY27 gross input-cost impact cut to INR 350-400 crore
rows.why: Full-year gross input-cost impact revised to 350-400 crore, slightly lower than May's estimate, after pricing, trade rationalisation and productivity mitigation, though input costs remain elevated.

rows.label: Karnataka and Maharashtra policy-led growth cycling
rows.why: Karnataka volumes grew 60%+ after the low-alcohol beer tax cut and gained ~250 bps share, but the base effect cycles from May-June next year, so state-driven growth should fade.
